new_statements.relation_note: Tone-box diagram only: ABCD 123-4 split, B=DL merger, P group (Proto-Tai voiced stops > plain voiceless).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tai Khang is catalogued as a P-group Southwestern Tai tone language whose proto-tones split two ways in every column by initial class (rows 1-2-3 vs row 4: A123/A4, B123/B4, C123/C4, DL123/DL4, DS123/DS4) with the B = DL coalescence (B123=DL123, B4=DL4) — the same box pattern the catalogue gives for Black Tai/White Tai (no. 29); this implies six tones on unchecked syllables. No pitch values, nothing on stress/accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none for this entry (the paper's caveats concern other dialects, e.g. note 5 on Muang Ka)
new_statements.identity_note: Entry 33 'Tai Khang' sits in the P-group (*ABCD 123-4) block next to '32. Tai Meuai, Tai Kuan' — the Khamkeut cluster (Schliesinger 2003: Tai Khang, Tai Guan, Tai Meuay of Khamkeut). Chamberlain 1986 note 11 independently states 'a Tai Khang language spoken in Muang Kam Keut in Khammouane province.. a P-group language', and Glottolog files tayk1238 under 'Southwestern Tai P'. Not the Phuan 'Tai Khang' of Muang Khang (Xieng Khouang; kang1282/[kyp]), which would be PH/Neua-Phuan. Caveat: note 3's list of dialects 'from the author's field notes' names Tai Meuai but omits Tai Khang and Tai Kuan (apparently an omission; no other source is credited for them).
